headline: Acquisition growth masks organic softness, margin pressure
summary_short: Total revenue rose 30.4% y/y to $1.68B on the closed Accession/RSC Topco acquisition, but Organic Revenue fell 0.7% and adjusted EBITDAC margin compressed 100bp to 35.7%; net income rose 24.7% y/y to $288M and diluted EPS was $0.84 (+7.7% y/y).
summary_long: Revenue growth of 30.4% y/y was almost entirely acquisition-driven (Accession/RSC Topco); Organic Revenue declined 0.7%, weighed down by an $18M litigation-related account loss. Adjusted EBITDAC margin fell 100bp y/y to 35.7% on acquisition/integration costs and higher interest expense from acquisition financing. GAAP diluted EPS of $0.84 (+7.7% y/y) was boosted by a $40M favorable earn-out revaluation; Adjusted diluted EPS of $1.07 (+3.9% y/y) strips that out along with near-doubled amortization ($110M vs $50M), and better reflects underlying performance. Cash fell to $918M from a year-ago balance inflated by stock/debt proceeds held in reserve for the acquisition, since deployed. No forward guidance was issued in this release.

drivers.explanation: Growth was almost entirely from acquisitions (primarily Accession/RSC Topco), which added $393M to core commissions & fees; underlying Organic Revenue fell 0.7%, including an $18M drag from litigation-related customer-account losses.
EBITDAC Margin - Adjusted fell from 36.7% to 35.7% as $31M of acquisition/integration costs and higher interest expense (from acquisition financing) weighed on margins.

GAAP diluted EPS growth was aided by a $40M favorable change in estimated acquisition earn-out payables; Adjusted EPS grew more slowly (+3.9%) once that item and near-doubled amortization ($110M vs $50M) tied to acquired intangibles were excluded.

The year-ago cash balance included stock-offering and senior-notes proceeds held in reserve ahead of closing the Accession acquisition; those proceeds have since been deployed, so the y/y comparison is not like-for-like.
CEO Powell Brown described the quarter's results as strong, citing momentum heading into the second half of 2026.
